completion-001.justification: The legacy ticket-completion-evidence.ts is I/O-bound: it reads git repos (execFileSync for cat-file, rev-parse, log), reads ticket frontmatter files from disk, and does git-log scan-based attribution. The new core evaluateCompletion is a pure function taking pre-computed booleans (shaExists, treeChanged, gateGreen). There is no pure legacy function that takes the same boolean inputs and produces a verdict — the legacy's decision logic (evaluateCompletionEvidence) operates on an EvidenceResult produced by readEvidence (which does I/O). Reconstructing the full I/O pipeline (git repo + frontmatter + scan) for each fixture would require building a mock of the entire pickle-rick extension runtime, which is infeasible without the extension's file/git infrastructure. The new core's completion logic is a simplification of the legacy's evidence-gathering pipeline, not a direct port of a pure function. Per architecture §5, completion is HARD feasibility; per VAL-CONF-008, it carries an explicit unverifiable-by-port annotation with justification and is NOT counted as a passing differential. Spec-conformance (the existing conformance test) validates the new core against fixture expected values.

gate-001.justification: The legacy convergence-gate.ts is lock/fs/git-bound: it uses withLock (file locking), spawnSync for git operations, reads baseline files from disk, runs gate commands (typecheck/lint/test) via child_process, and persists baseline state. The new core evaluateConvergenceGate is a pure function operating on pre-computed CheckResult[] and Finding[] arrays. There is no pure legacy function that takes the same inputs and produces a GateVerdict — the legacy's runGate function orchestrates the entire gate execution pipeline (lock, run commands, read/write baseline, compare). Reconstructing this pipeline for synthetic-git fixtures would require building a mock of the full gate execution infrastructure (lock manager, command runner, baseline file I/O). Only sub-pieces (subtractBaseline, filterByScope) are reusable as pure functions, but these are already validated by the new core's unit tests. Per architecture §5, convergence is HARD feasibility; per VAL-CONF-008, it carries an explicit unverifiable-by-port annotation with justification and is NOT counted as a passing differential. Spec-conformance validates the new core against fixture expected values.

prd-001.justification: The prd predicate has no file:line provenance in the legacy codebase. The legacy PRD handling is a markdown parser (parses PRD from markdown text into a structured model), while the new core evaluatePrd is an object validator (validates a pre-parsed PrdInput object). These are fundamentally different operations: the legacy parses text → object, the new core validates object → verdict. There is no legacy function that takes a PrdInput and produces a PrdVerdict. Per architecture §5, prd is UNVERIFIABLE-BY-PORT; per VAL-CONF-009, it carries an explicit unverifiable-by-port annotation with justification and falls back to spec-conformance. The prd fixtures are validated by the existing conformance test (spec-conformance), not by a legacy differential.
